lessons.title: What Is Pressure? Measuring the Invisible Push — Shoes, Scales, and Force Per Unit Area

quiz.prompt: A teacher presses a flat 300 g textbook onto her palm, then presses the tip of a sharpened pencil onto her palm with roughly the same force. Why does the pencil tip hurt more?
choices: The book spreads its mass out, so it has less weight
The pencil pushes on a much smaller area, so the pressure on the palm is greater
The pencil exerts a much larger force than the book
The pencil is sharp, so it has more mass concentrated at the tip
quiz.rationale: The force is about the same in both cases, but the pencil tip's contact area is tiny. Since P = F/A, a smaller area gives a much greater pressure.
quiz.placement: Part A — Pencil vs. Book Demonstration

quiz.prompt: In the shoe-pressure investigation, a pair traces a shoe sole on 1 cm² graph paper and counts 150 squares. What is this area in square metres (m²)?
choices: 1.5 m²
quiz.placement: Part B — Shoe Pressure Investigation, step (iii)–(iv) area conversion

quiz.prompt: A student has a mass of 50 kg (take g = 10 N/kg). The traced area of ONE of her shoe soles is 200 cm². Using half her body weight for one foot, what pressure does one shoe exert on the floor?
quiz.placement: Part B — Shoe Pressure Investigation, step (iv) calculate pressure

quiz.prompt: On the class data wall, flat sandals show pressures of about 16,000 Pa, while pointed heels show more than 100,000 Pa for people of similar weight. What best explains this pattern?
choices: Heels have a much smaller contact area, so the same weight produces a greater pressure
Heels have a larger contact area, which increases the pressure
People wearing heels push down with a much greater force
Sandals are lighter, so they reduce the person's weight
quiz.rationale: For roughly the same force (body weight), P = F/A means a smaller contact area, like a heel, gives a much larger pressure.

quiz.prompt: Which of these is the correct SI unit of pressure?
choices: Pascal (Pa), equal to one newton per square centimetre (N/cm²)
Newton (N), equal to one kilogram metre per second squared
Kilogram per square metre (kg/m²)
Pascal (Pa), equal to one newton per square metre (N/m²)
quiz.rationale: Pressure is force (N) divided by area (m²), so its SI unit is the pascal: 1 Pa = 1 N/m².
quiz.placement: Explain: formal definition P = F/A and note frame

quiz.prompt: A 90 kg maize bag (take g = 10 N/kg) is placed on a wooden pallet in a warehouse in Eldoret. The pallet has 4 legs, each with a base area of 25 cm². What pressure does EACH leg exert on the floor?
choices: 9 Pa
36 Pa
quiz.placement: Explain: Extension Problem 1 (maize bag on pallet in Eldoret)

quiz.prompt: A Maasai elder leans on a rungu with a tip area of 2 cm², using a force of 150 N. A nurse at Kenyatta National Hospital uses a crutch with a flat base of 50 cm², also with a force of 150 N. Which statement is correct?
choices: The crutch exerts the greater pressure because its area is larger, so the rungu is safer
The rungu exerts the greater pressure, so the crutch is safer for a soft floor
Both exert the same pressure because the force is the same
The rungu exerts less pressure because its area is smaller, so it is safer
quiz.rationale: Rungu: 150 ÷ 0.0002 = 750,000 Pa; crutch: 150 ÷ 0.005 = 30,000 Pa. The larger crutch base spreads the same force, giving lower pressure and less damage to a soft floor.

quiz.prompt: A sealed plastic jerrycan stands on a bench surrounded by air. In which direction does the air outside push on the jerrycan?
choices: Downward on the top face only
Inward on the top and sides, but not on the bottom
Inward on all six faces: top, bottom and all four sides
Outward from all faces, away from the jerrycan
quiz.rationale: Atmospheric pressure acts on every exposed face of an object, so the outside air pushes inward on all faces, not just downward from above.
quiz.placement: Model: revising the jerrycan force diagram with arrows on all six faces

quiz.prompt: A sealed jerrycan full of air does not collapse, but after some air is removed from inside it crumples inward. Which explanation is correct?
choices: The pressure inside became less than the pressure outside, so the outward push no longer balanced the inward push
The remaining air inside sucked the walls inward
Removing the air made the plastic walls weaker
The air outside became heavier when air was removed from inside
quiz.rationale: Before, inside and outside air pressures were balanced. Removing air lowered the inside pressure, so the greater outside pressure pushed the walls in.
quiz.placement: Model: sentence frame 'Before the air was removed… After air was removed…'
